correctness.rationale: Rogers arXiv:0704.2438 v4, Theorem 3.1 Eq. (3.4), supplies the exact generating series. Coefficient extraction is algebraically exact and was independently compared for 80 terms. Legendre gives valuation 2(n-2k)+4s2(k)+s2(n-2k)-s2(n+k). At n=2^r-1, reindex k=2^(r-1)-1-j. For 0<=j<=2^(r-1)-2 the valuation is 3r+4j-1-3s2(j)+s2(j+1). It equals 3r at j=0 and exceeds 3r by at least j-1+s2(j+1)>=1 at every j>=1. The k=0 endpoint has valuation 2^(r+1)-2>3r for r>=3. Unique minimum of nonnegative integer sum proves exact total valuation. Direct calculations confirm finite boundaries r=1 has 2, r=2 has 8, and r=3..9 have 3r; finite tests not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Full relevant primary sections were compared by mathematical implications. Rogers and Chan-Zudilin give transformed binomial sums, not Mersenne 2-adic exponent. Malik-Straub proves mod-2 Lucas and eventual mod-4 divisibility only. Beluhov proves w4(n)>=3s2(n), with sharpness iff no adjacent 1s, which converts to v2(D_n)>=2s2(n); its n=2^r-1 case has a strict lower bound but no equality formula. OEIS A002895 lists Domb values and formulas but no exact valuation at all Mersenne indices. Scientific-result searches identify a shifted generalized Domb sum supercongruence on other families; it does not imply the current claim. Unknown unpublished or unindexed stronger valuation theorem remains possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed theorem or a stronger general congruence for the Domb sequence may imply the precise all-ones valuation; current searches do not eliminate this possibility.
A highly specialized derivation from Rogers or Chan-Zudilin might have appeared without explicit Mersenne terminology. The existing source formulas themselves are not asserted original.
Self-review is not an independent literature audit.

value.rationale: Domb numbers count diamond-lattice closed polygons, and a sharp prime-power divisibility threshold of their terms is a natural arithmetic invariant. The binary all-ones indices are a distinguished infinite family used in studying digital carry patterns and lower-bound exceptions. Exact exponent 3r is not implied by the known fixed-modulus congruences or the general lower bound, reveals a simple linear growth law, and is established through an unexpectedly unique minimal Rogers summand. That structural explanation and exact natural-index classification are useful without requiring a general theorem for every n. It is not an arbitrary numeric slice or an experimental extrapolation.
